title: TrueNorth shared definitions
description: Reusable $defs shared by every TrueNorth content schema. This file defines no root shape; it is referenced, never validated against.

id.title: Identifier
id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier, unique within its collection. Unbranded: a property that $refs this def is a plain string in the port type. When the value names an entity the id vocabulary covers, $ref the branded def below instead.

levelId.title: Level id
levelId.description: Names a level document, `content/levels/<id>.json`. Mirrored by the branded `LevelId` in app/domain/ids.ts.

questId.title: Quest id
questId.description: Names a quest document. Mirrored by the branded `QuestId`.

questionId.title: Question id
questionId.description: Names a question in a subject's bank. Mirrored by the branded `QuestionId`.

subjectId.title: Subject id
subjectId.description: One of the ten Discover Canada subjects; also the question-bank key. Mirrored by the branded `SubjectId`.

characterId.title: Character id
characterId.description: Names a character document. Mirrored by the branded `CharacterId`.

poiId.title: Point-of-interest id
poiId.description: Names a landmark a player can engage on a level. Mirrored by the branded `PoiId`.

localeCode.title: Locale code
localeCode.description: A supported UI locale. EN and FR ship from the first commit. Mirrored by the branded `LocaleCode`.

isoInstant.title: ISO instant
isoInstant.description: ISO-8601 instant, as persisted in save data and in content `asOf` fields. Mirrored by the branded `IsoInstant`.

localizedText.title: Localized text
localizedText.description: A string in every supported locale. Both EN and FR are mandatory, which is how ADR-0003's "missing EN or FR text" clause is enforced per document rather than per string table.

factSource.title: Fact source
factSource.description: Where a claim about Canada comes from. Written by the content-author agent, never by the verifier (ADR-0003). The same block backs a question, a landmark blurb and a line of NPC dialogue, because a wrong fact is equally wrong wherever a player reads it.

sourceId.description: Which cached source this came from: the `id` of a content/sources/<id>.json manifest. Without it a chapter title and a hash are strings pointing at nothing, and ADR-0003's whole mechanism - a status granted for a hash, invalidated when the hash moves - has no second end. It is also what lets a gate read the source's knownStaleness list and insist that a question drawn from a region known to be out of date is marked volatile.

chapter.description: Chapter or section heading, exactly as it appears in the cited source. Must match one of that source manifest's chapters[].title.

page.description: Page the claim was read from, when the source is paginated. Must fall inside the cited chapter's page range, which is what `sourceChapter.endPage` makes checkable - and it is what lets a page-grain staleness flag be evaluated per question instead of forcing every question in a long chapter volatile.

quote.description: The passage the author read the claim from, copied exactly. Author-owned, and not the same field as `factVerification.evidence`: this one says where the wording came from, and the verifier's says what entails the ANSWER - for a question with distractors those are often different sentences. Copied exactly because it must be a contiguous substring of the cached extraction at the recorded hash, which is a check that catches a fabricated citation before any verifier runs.

sourceHash.description: SHA-256 of what the verifier actually read: the manifest's extractedTextSha256 when the source has an extraction, and its sha256 otherwise. Hashing what was read rather than what was downloaded is the difference that matters - a re-extraction with a different tool changes the text a claim was checked against without touching the document.

asOf.description: When the source was fetched. Against a maintained source, a volatile item whose asOf exceeds 180 days is quarantined. Against a source whose register records it as unrevised, the 180-day clock moves to that register's `liveChecks[].checkedAt` and quarantines the SOURCE rather than each question under it - one fetch instead of N re-verifications of a page that cannot have changed, and it still fails closed. ADR-0016.

volatile.description: True when the fact can change WITHOUT NOTICE - office holders, dates, counts. It is a property of the FACT, written by the author, and it deliberately says nothing about the source. What a volatile item's periodic re-check consists of is a property of the SOURCE, and lives in that register's `liveChecks` and `knownStaleness[].upstream` (ADR-0016). Conflating the two is what produced the defect: `volatile` was read as 're-verify every run and quarantine at 180 days', which is right against a maintained source and is busywork against one that will never be revised, where the re-fetch can only ever return the same wrong text.

factVerification.title: Fact verification
factVerification.description: The block the content-verifier agent writes, and the only block it may write (ADR-0003). Four statuses: `unverified` before a check has run, `verified` when every check passed for this sourceHash, `rejected` when the verifier's judgement failed and the text goes back to the author, `quarantined` when a granted status was later invalidated by source drift or age and it goes back to the verifier. `rejected` and `quarantined` are both excluded from the build and differ only in who owns the next move.

model.description: The model that granted the status, so a bad verifier run can be identified later.

checkedAt.description: When the check ran. null while the status is unverified.

sourceHash.description: The sourceHash the status was granted for; a mismatch with the source block invalidates it. Empty string while unverified.

evidence.description: The passage from the cited section that entails the claim, quoted exactly. Empty is only tolerable when nothing has been granted.

allOf.$comment: The null form is the ONLY legal shape of an unverified block, so "an author wrote nothing but the zero value" is checkable by validate-content instead of only by reading a diff. That is what makes task 1.17's git-history gate a single sentence - an author-authored commit may write a verification object only in this form and may never change one that exists - with no per-field carve-out. Only property names this object already declares appear here (ADR-0007).

ADR-0003's CI clause, stated in the schema so make validate-content fails on it and not only verify-content: a verified status with no quoted passage is an assertion, and this project does not accept assertions. The conditional only names properties this object already declares, so it adds no unmirrored shape (ADR-0007).

factClaim.title: Fact claim
factClaim.description: Attached to player-facing prose outside the question bank - a landmark blurb, a line of NPC dialogue - so that ADR-0003 governs every sentence stating something about Canada, not only the ones on a question card. `factual` is the author's declaration that this text asserts a fact; it is required rather than optional so the judgement is recorded for every line instead of defaulting to unchecked. When it is true, source and verification must both be present and the verifier treats the text exactly as it treats a question.

factual.description: Does this text state a fact about Canada? Greetings, instructions and flavour are false; anything a player could repeat in the citizenship test is true.

allOf.$comment: A claimed fact must be sourced and checked. Only property names this object already declares appear here (ADR-0007).

nationName.title: Nation name
nationName.description: One nation, in the form that nation uses for itself: Mi'kmaq, Algonquin Anishinaabe, Haudenosaunee (Kanien'keha:ka), Nunatsiavummiut, Metis Nation of Alberta. The pattern is a deny-list, applied case-insensitively and ignoring surrounding whitespace, of the category words that are not nations - Indigenous, Aboriginal, First Nations, Inuit, Metis, tribal, traditional, unspecified, generic, n/a, TBD and the rest. docs/content-review.md 3.1 makes those a build failure rather than a warning, because "a generic Indigenous person" is the failure this rule exists to prevent and a vague value here is that failure wearing the field's name. Two nations may be named only when the depiction is explicitly of two; two names used as hedging is the vague value spelled longer, and no gate can tell the difference - only a reader can.

nationSource.title: Nation source
nationSource.description: Evidence that a named nation was copied from somewhere real. Per docs/content-review.md 3.2 the source must be the nation's own published material - its government, its cultural centre, its language authority - or a registry that nation is listed in. Same author/verifier split as a question: the author writes publisher, url, sourceHash and asOf; the verifier writes the verification block and nothing else. What this proves is narrow and is stated so nobody reads it as more: that the name appears on a page that was fetched and hashed. It does not prove the name is right, that the nation would recognise the spelling, or that this is the nation actually depicted. Only a Tier 3 reviewer checks those, and this project has none.

publisher.description: Whose material this is, named: the nation's government, cultural centre, language authority, or the registry.

sourceHash.description: SHA-256 of the cached page under content/sources/, empty until the verifier has fetched it.

communityReview.title: Community review
communityReview.description: Whether the nation depicted has been asked, and what they said. docs/content-review.md 1 extends ADR-0003's separation of duties one step: no agent may grant cultural sign-off, ever, for any reason - an agent may write status "not-sought" and nothing else. THE SCHEMA CANNOT ENFORCE THAT AND MUST NOT BE READ AS DOING SO: a schema constrains a value, not its author, and any schema that permits "granted" at all permits an agent to write it. What the schema does is raise the cost and change the shape of the lie - a fabricated sign-off must now name a person, an organisation, a date and a scope, which is a specific and checkable falsehood rather than a flag flip, and "not-sought" is forced to carry no names at all so a review cannot be half-claimed. The author rule itself needs a gate that reads git history: verify-content must fail when a commit authored by an agent moves status away from not-sought. That is slice 1 task 1.17's, and until it exists this block is enforced by review.

reviewer.description: The person who reviewed it, named. Null when nothing has been sought.

scope.description: What exactly was reviewed. A sign-off on a hat is not a sign-off on a character.

allOf.$comment: not-sought carries no names: a review cannot be half-claimed, and an agent writing the only status it may write cannot smuggle a person into the record. Every other status must name a person, an organisation, a date and a scope. Only property names this object already declares appear here (ADR-0007).

vec2.title: Vec2
vec2.description: A 2D vector: a point, size or scroll factor in design-resolution pixels (1080x1920).
